In  default, 1 year R.I. more.
All the sentences have been ordered to run concurrently.
Heard Ms. Supriya Upasane, learned counsel for the appellants.
Also heard Mr. Waseem Miyan, learned Panel Lawyer, appearing for the State/respondent on IA No. 1 of 2022, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellants.
Learned counsel for the convict/appellants has argued that the appellants have been falsely implicated in the present case.

The appellants are alleged to have committed forceful sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix who was a minor and thereafter committed her murder by strangulating and causing injuries on her head and thereafter cut her wrist with an axe in order to cause disappearance of evidence.
Mr. Upasne submits that the instant case rests on circumstantial evidence and there appears to be only evidence of last seen by PW-1 and PW-8.
It is submitted that the allegation rape was found to be committed on the deceased was found to be false one as no semen was found on the private part of the deceased.

She lastly argued that the appellant is in custody since 11.10.2018 and the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more for its final disposal, hence he prays that the appellants be enlarged on bail.

The learned counsel for the State/respondent has objected the bail application and submits that the deceased was forcefully gang-raped by the appellants and thereafter, she was murdered and in order to cause disappearance of the evidence, they had cut the wrist of the deceased and concealed the body in a residential school.
One of the inmate of the school had informed the school authority that a body was lying in the school premises in a decayed condition.
Thereafter an FIR has been lodged and investigation proceeded and just after three days, the appellants were arrested.
The medical report of the appellants were found to be positive.

Therefore, the learned Trial Court, after appreciating the evidence on record and after examining the cross-examination of the witnesses,
came to the conclusion regarding guilty of the accused, which is just and proper.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly considering the fact that the deceased was gang-raped and the FSL report of the appellants were found to be positive which supports the case of the prosecution, at this stage, we deem it appropriate to reject the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail at this stage.
Accordingly, IA No. 1 of 2022 stands disposed of.
It transpires from the record that the matter is ripe for final hearing.
Let the matters be listed for final hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) (Ramesh Sinha)
